text: Creates scatter plot comparing raw variable values corresponding normalised indicator values produced ec_normalise_dev(). plot intended simple diagnostic visualisation tool evaluating ecological normalisation functions. text: variable Numeric vector normalised. x0 Numeric. Reference value corresponding indicator value 0. Can single value vector length variable. Defaults 0. x60 Numeric NULL. Optional reference value corresponding indicator value 0.6. Can single value vector length variable. supplied, fun = "linear", piecewise linear normalisation used. x60 can also combined fun = "sigmoid". x100 Numeric. Reference value corresponding indicator value 1. Can single value vector length variable. x60h Numeric NULL. Currently unused/reserved future support two-sided normalisation upper x60 reference value. x0h Numeric NULL. Optional high-end reference value corresponding indicator value 0 two-sided normalisation. Can single value vector length variable. fun Character. Transformation function applied normalisation. One "linear" (transformation), "sigmoid", "exponential convex", "exponential concave". Defaults "linear". convex_exponent Numeric. Exponent used fun = "exponential convex". Defaults 0.5. concave_exponent Numeric. Exponent used fun = "exponential concave". Defaults 2. truncation Logical. TRUE (default), normalised values clamped interval [0, 1]. FALSE, values outside reference range linearly extrapolated may fall 0 1. Disabling truncation supported fun = "linear".

title: ec_normalise — ec_normalise
text: Normalises (rescales) numeric vector values 0 1 using reference values. function supports linear increasing, linear decreasing, two-sided, piecewise linear normalisation, exponential sigmoid functions. reference parameters (x0, x60, x100, x60h, x0h) may supplied either single values vectors length variable. vector reference values used, relationship x0 x100 must consistent observations; , observations must either x0 < x100 must x0 > x100. default, values outside reference range truncated interval [0, 1]. Set truncation = FALSE instead extrapolate linear mapping beyond reference range, returning values 0 1. available fun = "linear", non-linear transformations otherwise produce NaN negative extrapolated values. Two-sided normalisation defined x60 values currently supported. Exponential transformations currently supported x60 used.
